chunk_findings.detail: The new guard preserves an existing end only when `sess.how` is non-empty, but a normal `session.ended` event can be processed without `how` (the summary-only `session end --summary` path, and any historical `session.ended` event after the new field was introduced). The handler then sets `ended_at` while leaving `how` empty, contradicting the documented invariant that `how` is `""` only while open. A later bare summary event sees `not sess.how` and re-enters the branch, moving `ended_at` to the later event's timestamp. For example, process `session.ended` at T1 with `{"summary":"first"}` followed by `session.ended` at T2 with `{"summary":"second"}`: after the first event the session is ended at T1, but after the second it is ended at T2, so a summary-only update changes the end time instead of only updating `summary`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/sessions.py:242-245 (`_h_session_ended`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new optional-field refresh only verifies that the existing hook contains the fields emitted by `_entry_options`; it never verifies that undesired optional fields are absent, and the update line `{**h, "type": "command", "command": wanted, **opts}` merges desired options without deleting stale ones. `hookwriters` requests synchronous hooks for all non-`stop` events and `timeout=30`/no background for `session_end`. If a ddflow `session_end` hook already contains a stale `"background": true` (for example copied from the stop hook or left by an earlier install), the `all(h.get(k) == v for k, v in opts.items())` check can still pass because only the requested `timeout` is compared, so `add_hook` returns “already” and leaves the SessionEnd hook background/async. The harness may then not wait for the SessionEnd hook to write the session-end record, even though the current install requests a synchronous 30-second hook.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/claudehooks.py:add_hook

chunk_findings.detail: `previous_lines` filters sessions to those with `s.prompts or s.notes` before choosing the latest closed session, so it can report an older session as the “previous session” when the actual latest closed session has only a summary. For example, agent A has session `S1` closed at 10:00 with a prompt/note, then session `S2` closed at 11:00 by `close_ended` or `session end --summary done` with no prompts or notes. The comprehension excludes `S2`, `max(closed, key=ended_at)` returns `S1`, and the next session is shown `## Previous session (S1, ended 10:00)` with stale hand-over data even though `S2` was the previous session.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_lifecycle.py:245

chunk_findings.detail: `test_previous_session_is_shown_fenced_and_bounded` still requires the hand-over text to contain the HTML-escaped form `<ddflow-record` after a previous prompt containing `<ddflow-record>x...`. The Round-2 fixes listed for this change do not include escaping the previous-session prompt/note, and the prior probe showed the previous-session renderer emits the stored text raw. Running this test therefore reaches line 156 with `text` containing raw `<ddflow-record` and no `<ddflow-record`, raising `AssertionError`; the planted tag is not neutralized.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_interrupted.py:156

chunk_findings.detail: After a phantom `session.started`, the refresh is `events, st = log.read_all(), fold(log.read_all(), strict=False)`, so the two snapshots are separate locked operations. A second writer that appends a `session.note` (or a `session.ended`) between those reads leaves `events` without that event while `st` already includes it. `record_inflight` / `close_ended` then dedupe or close from disagreeing inputs: the next Stop treats the note as unseen and appends the same in-flight note again, which is the duplicate this round claims to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup/hooks.py:331

chunk_findings.detail: A write during lease grace permanently exempts the session from interrupted close. `lease.live(now, grace_s)` treats the hold as live until `renewed_at + ttl_s + grace_s`, but both lapse sources record only the TTL end (`renewed_at + ttl_s`, or `at + ttl_s`). `find_dead` then requires `_epoch(last) <= max(hits)`. Given ttl end t=100, grace 30, a `session.note` at t=110, and a crash at t=115, at now=200 the agent has no live lease so the session is dead, but hits=[100] and 110 <= 100 is false, so `close_interrupted` never appends `session.ended`. The same note keeps winning on every later SessionStart.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_lifecycle.py:_lapses

chunk_findings.detail: The “previous session” is not the latest ended session of this agent. The candidate filter requires `s.prompts or s.notes`, then `max(..., key=ended_at)` runs only on that subset. Given session A ended at 10:00 with a prompt, and session B (same agent) ended at 11:00 via `close_ended` with summary `session ended (logout)` and no prompt or note (`holding nothing` writes nothing), `previous_lines` fences A and labels it the previous session. B is the previous session; its summary is never shown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_lifecycle.py:previous_lines
